text:
ashwin: Ran a canary vs prod sweep for model v3.1 focused on kernel selection + batching heuristics. Short summary: chat-stream route shows a token-level median increase of ~6ms and p95 spike ~14ms. Uploading traces and waterfall snapshots.

perf-bot: Canary comparison report: route=chat-stream, traffic=5% canary, samples=6.2k tokens. p50_delta=+5.8ms, p95_delta=+14.2ms, p99_delta=+37.6ms. flame_url=https://perf.redwood/internal/compare/1812349999 (private).

maria: Any change to KV cache behavior? That pattern smells like more cache misses or extra memcpy on small sequences. Did the canary pick a different kv-path kernel?

dash: Uploaded token-waterfall SVG and a small profiler dump to the thread. Key observation: short prefix tokens (1-8) dominate the median regression. Longer sequences converge.

devon: KV hitrate: baseline=95.1% -> canary=86.8% on the chat-stream tests (same request mix). TTL/prefetch didn't change in config, but kernel selector now favours fused-attn for seq<=64 which may bypass optimized KV-read path.

ashwin: Reproduced locally with microbench harness. Patch that switches to fused-attn shows +5-7ms for seq<=32, but improves throughput for batched long sequences. So it's an optimization tradeoff.

oleg: Batcher notes: continuous-scheduler saw increased microbursting. Sample log: `[batcher] sched=continuous batch_ms=8 avg_tokens=4 burst=1.8x` — small batches amplify kernel overhead. Could be amplifying the new kernel's startup cost.

ashwin: Here's the kernel selector snippet used in canary:
```
kernel_selector:
  fused_attention_threshold: 64
  prefer_fused: true
  cost_model: 'latency-v2'
```

maria: If fused path bypasses KV fastpath, that explains lower hit-effective throughput. Any way to route chat-stream to the old kv-optimized kernel during rollout? We should avoid a full rollback if possible.

devon: Quick mitigation: add route override to prefer kernel `optimized-kv-path` for `route=chat-stream` until we tune thresholds. Patch suggestion:
```
routes:
  - match: chat-stream
    override_kernel: optimized-kv-path
```

hannah: Dashboard notes: Route-centric KPIs show the chat-stream SLO breach window at 03:14 UTC when canary reached 3% traffic. Rollout heatmap flagged p95 > SLO for 12m. Suggest we pause rollout and apply route override.

ashwin: I pushed a hotfix flag to the canary cluster to force `optimized-kv-path` on chat-stream. Re-running the compare now.

perf-bot: Re-check complete: route=chat-stream, after-hotfix p50_delta=+0.4ms, p95_delta=+1.2ms, p99_delta=+5.6ms. KV hitrate returned to 94.6%. Canary still useful for long-seq throughput gains but not safe for chat-stream default.

oleg: Long-term: we should update the kernel cost model to include per-route token distribution and batch size. Current static threshold is too coarse. Proposal: per-route cost_model + dynamic threshold that adapts to observed batch_ms and kv_hit_rate.

maria: Agreed. Can we add token-level KPI breakdown to the rollout dashboard? Want p50/p95 by token-position buckets (1-4,5-16,17-64,65+). That would catch these regressions earlier.

hannah: Adding to roadmap: `rollout-dashboard#token-slices` — will prototype next sprint. For now, patch is in and canary paused for chat-stream.

ashwin: Notes for the perf doc: - Kernel selector needs route-aware override - Batcher tuning to reduce microburst for chat workloads - Enhance KV instrumentation (per-request kv_path taken) - Add token-position buckets to rollout dashboards

devon: I'll open a PR with the override + a new metric `kv_path` tag in traces. cc @maria for acceptance tests.

perf-bot: Canary verdict: regression flagged -> rollout paused -> auto-fallback NOT triggered (manual patch applied). Tickets: PERF-4123 (kernel cost-model), PERF-4124 (dashboard token-slices), PERF-4125 (batcher burst smoothing).

ashwin: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: devon will land PR, maria will add unit/integration checks for kv_path, hannah will prototype dashboard tile. We'll re-run the canary after cost-model update. :thumbsup:
